user.title: Add a ShowPilot Player
user.description: The Player's address, as you open it in a browser (for example `showpilot.local` or `192.168.1.60`). Add `:port` if it doesn't use port 80. Next, you allow Home Assistant on the Player.

data_description.host: Name or IP address of the ShowPilot Player

password.title: Sign in to the Player
password.description: {host} runs an older ShowPilot Player that can't pair. Enter a user name and password from Settings → Users on the Player (leave the user name empty if it only has an admin password). Update the Player to 0.13.1 or newer to pair instead.

zeroconf_confirm.title: ShowPilot Player found
zeroconf_confirm.description: Add **{name}** ({host}) to Home Assistant? Next, you allow Home Assistant on the Player.

reauth_confirm.title: Pair {name} again
reauth_confirm.description: The Player no longer accepts Home Assistant (its access key was deleted, or a password changed). Press Submit, then press **Allow** on the Player's page.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure {name}
reconfigure.description: Check the address, then press Submit and **Allow** on the Player's page. Home Assistant gets a new access key of its own; your entities and automations stay as they are.

pair_denied.title: Not allowed
pair_denied.description: The Player said no, or nobody pressed Allow within 10 minutes. Press Submit to ask {host} again.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach a ShowPilot Player at that address.
error.not_player: That address doesn't answer like a ShowPilot Player.
error.too_old: This Player's software is too old for Home Assistant. Update it to 0.11.0 or newer (Settings → Updates on the Player).
error.unknown: Unexpected error; see the Home Assistant log.
error.pair_refused: The Player refused to pair. Pairing works only on the same network as the Player, not through Public access.

abort.already_configured: This Player is already set up.
abort.not_player: The device found doesn't identify itself as a ShowPilot Player.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Done. Home Assistant has a new access key.
abort.wrong_device: That address belongs to a different ShowPilot Player.
abort.too_old: This Player's software is too old for Home Assistant. Update it to 0.11.0 or newer (Settings → Updates on the Player).
abort.unknown: Unexpected error; see the Home Assistant log.

progress.pair:
Open the Player's page ({host}) on any device. A box says that Home Assistant wants to control it: check it shows the code **{code}**, then press **Allow**.

This waits for up to 10 minutes.

trigger_type.show_starting: Show starting (schedule opened or Start Main Show fade began)
trigger_type.show_stopping: Show stopping (after this song or loop)
trigger_type.show_resumed: Show resumed after the Player restarted

start_playlist.name: Start playlist
start_playlist.description: Start a playlist on the Player (stops what's playing).

playlist.name: Playlist
playlist.description: Playlist name as on the Player.

insert_playlist.name: Insert playlist
insert_playlist.description: Play a playlist in the middle of the show, then carry on.

playlist.name: Playlist
playlist.description: Playlist name as on the Player.

when.name: When
when.description: After the current song, or right away.

run_command.name: Run command
run_command.description: Run an FPP-style command on the Player (the same commands as its Commands page).

args.name: Arguments
args.description: List of arguments, in the order the command takes them.

run_preset.name: Run command preset
run_preset.description: Run one of the Player's command presets.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: Preset name as on the Player's Commands page.

start_main_show.name: Start Main Show
start_main_show.description: Fade out the pre-show music and lights, then start the main show playlist (Background music settings on the Player).

stop_after_song.name: Stop after this song
stop_after_song.description: Let the current song finish, play the lead-out, then stop.
